messages.subject: Creating UGP for custom CDF
parts:
Hi.

On Fri, Feb 22, 2008 at 11:50 AM, Jin Peng Szatkiewicz
<jin.sza...@jax.org> wrote:
> Also, as to the annotation of the SNPs, I have created a file
> containing 3 columns: probe_id, chromosome, physical bp. How should I
> use that? Thanks for your advice and all of your help!

You need to create an UGP file containing a (unit, group, position)
map that is specific to your CDF and maps each unit one-to-one in
order. Please see my previous reply on how to do that.

/Henrik

>
>
> Jin

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Creating UGP for custom CDF
parts: Hi.

On Mon, Feb 25, 2008 at 12:01 PM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
> I understand that your program can import APT total CN estimates. I
> wonder if a reverse action can be done. That is if you can output the
> total CN values to an output text files after low-level processing
> (Fragment length adjustment). That would allow one to generate UGP
> file in correct order and also allow one to use the total CN
> elsewhere.

The order of the rows in a UGP table/file is uniquely specified by the
order of the units in the corresponding CDF. There is one UGP file
per CDF. Please see below comments on how to create a UGP file (from
my reply in thread 'can I analyze custom array?', 2008-02-21):

<quote> ("with some minor corrections")
> You will need to setup a so called Unit Genome Position (UGP)
> annotation file which contains a (unit, chromosome, position) map
> specific to given CDF. If you have a NetAffx containing this
> information, you can follow the instructions on how it was done for
> the GenomeWideSNP_6,Full.cdf:
>
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/genomewidesnp-6---miscellaneous
>
> If you don't have a NetAffx-like data file, you can still allocate an
> empty UGP file, e.g.
>
> ugp <- AromaUgpFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="JP20080221");
> print(ugp)
>
> and populate the UGP map yourself, e.g.
>
> # Set the chromosomes for the first seven units
> ugp[1:7,1] <- c(1,1,2,2,3,4,5)
>
> # ...and their physical positions
> ugp[1:7,2] <- c(13410,43031,10322,10323,34303,12304,40335)
>
> Note that the rows in the UGP table should map one-to-one to the units
> in the CDF, e.g.
>
> unitName <- "SNP_A-123231"
> unit <- indexOf(cdf, unitName)
> stopifnot(getUnitNames(cdf, unit), unitName)
>
> ...and the genome position for this unit should be:
>
> print(ugp[unit,])
</quote>

When you understand how to create an UGP as above, you'll see that it
does not make sense to go via an APT file. An Affymetrix APT file
contains CN estimates but an UGP file in independent of measurement
data as it only contains annotation data. They are non-related
concepts. I also don't think that Affymetrix have specified a rule how
to order the units in an APT file (though it is likely that it use the
same order as the CDF).

Hope this explains how you create an UGP file and how to populate it
with data for your chip type.

Cheers

/Henrik

Hmm... that one took a while to figure out because I could not
reproduce it on either Windows on Linux, but I found and old R v2.5.1
on OSX where I got the same error and could fix it (details below for
the record). I learned something today.

I've uploaded a patch which (I hope) solves the problem. Install and
apply the patch by:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

If you then can do the following without errors, you should be able to
build you UGP file:

> xmlToList(listToXml(list(a=2)))
$a
[1] "2"

Let us know if it helps.

DETAILS: The reason is probably obvious when you know it and know a
bit of ASCII, about locales etc. This is what I learned:

> regexpr("[a-Z]", "foo")
Error in regexpr(pattern, text, extended, fixed, useBytes) :
invalid regular expression '[a-Z]'
> regexpr("[a-zA-Z]", "foo")
[1] 1
attr(,"match.length")
[1] 1
> regexpr("[A-z]", "foo")
[1] 1
attr(,"match.length")
[1] 1

In ASCII, the upper-case letters comes before the lower-case ones, and
for some reason does the native regexpr complain about pattern 'a-Z',
which have to be 'A-z'. On Windows and Linux this is more forgiving.

Cheers

/Henrik
